title: Poreč with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Costs & Verdict
metaDescription: Poreč with a dog in 2027: official dog beaches, restaurants, old town rules, hotel dog fees, best months, vets and EU pet passport rules for driving in.
content:
## Dog Beaches in Poreč

Poreč promotes itself as a pet-friendly destination and lists about 12 dog beaches in the area, most of them close to pet-friendly hotels, campsites and apartments. Many have a water bowl, a shelter or kennel, waste bins and a dog toilet.

**Špadići Dog Beach** opened on 7 June 2018 and was the first official dog beach in Poreč. It lies east of the Zelena Laguna resort. It has water and feeding stations, dog toilets and bins. Dogs must have a vaccination certificate showing valid rabies protection.

**Brulo Dog Beach** is also in the Zelena Laguna area, between the Brulo and Delfin beaches. **Lanterna Dog Beach** is at the Lanterna campsite north-west of town, and the resort has a dog exercise area. **Camp Istra** and the bay near Bijela Uvala are other established options. **Polidor**, between Funtana and Bijela Uvala, has a pebble beach with designated dog areas and rental loungers. **Istralandia** has a dog beach about 20 km from Poreč.

Rules differ by operator, so read the sign at each entrance. Dogs should stay on a leash outside marked dog zones.

## Are Dogs Allowed on Other Beaches?

No, not on regular public beaches. Many of Poreč's beaches hold Blue Flag status, and dogs are not allowed on them during the season. Rocky coves and pine-shaded shoreline along the Brulo, Plava Laguna and Zelena Laguna hotel belts are used by dog owners for sea entry, but signage can change. Stick to marked dog beaches in July and August, when enforcement is strictest.

## Dogs in Poreč Old Town

The old town is easy with a leashed dog. The waterfront promenade and the stone lanes of the Roman street grid (Decumanus) are open to leashed dogs. Pavement stone gets hot in summer, so walk in the morning or after 19:00. Dogs are not normally admitted inside the UNESCO-listed Euphrasian Basilica, so one adult should wait outside while the other visits. Leashes are mandatory, and breeds on Croatia's restricted list must also wear a muzzle.

## Restaurants, Cafés and Shops

The local tourist board says dogs are welcome in about 99% of Poreč's restaurants, bars and shops. In practice, dogs are accepted on terraces and in many indoor spaces at the owner's discretion. They are not allowed in food-preparation areas or supermarkets. Ask before sitting, and bring a travel mat and bowl.

## National Parks, Ferries and Catamarans

Croatian national parks set their own rules. Many restrict or ban dogs in sensitive zones, and others require a leash at all times. Check the individual park's website before booking tickets. Istria's coastal and forest trails outside protected parks, including the Parenzana cycling and walking route, are better dog territory.

On ferries and catamarans, dogs are generally carried on a leash, often with a muzzle, and may need a ticket. Some operators limit dogs to the outer deck. Rules vary by company and season, so confirm by email before travelling and carry the pet passport.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog

Pet fees in Croatia typically run from about €5 to €15 per night in apartments and hotels, with a cleaning fee on some listings. Campsites usually charge a daily dog rate, often €5 to €10 in high season. Some private apartments allow dogs free of charge. Many listings cap the number and size of dogs, so state breed and weight when booking. Lanterna Premium Camping Resort is a notable option, with its dog exercise area.

## Summer Heat and Best Months

July and August bring daytime highs around 30 °C and above. Asphalt and stone surfaces get hot enough to burn paws, and shade on dog beaches is limited. **The best months with a dog are May, June, September and early October.** Sea temperatures stay swimmable until about early October, crowds are lower, and fewer beach restrictions are enforced. In midsummer, walk before 09:00 and after 19:00, and never leave a dog in a parked car.

## Vet Basics

Poreč has a veterinary hospital offering treatment, vaccinations, emergency surgery and dog boarding. A small clinic, Veterinarska Ambulanta K&K, also operates in town. For night emergencies, a 24/7 vet may be around 60 km away, so save the on-call number before the first beach day. Tick prevention is advisable for Istria's forests and meadows, and Mediterranean sandfly and heartworm protection is a good idea in summer. Ask your own vet which products fit your dog.

## EU Pet Passport Rules for Driving In

- The dog needs an ISO 11784/11785 microchip.
- The microchip must be implanted before, or on the same day as, the rabies vaccination.
- Wait 21 days after the primary rabies vaccination before travelling.
- Carry the EU pet passport issued by an authorised vet. From 22 April 2026, passports are issued only to owners whose main home is in an EU country.
- Croatia is in Schengen, so there is no routine border stop from Slovenia or Hungary. Carry documents anyway, since checks can happen.
- Travellers from Great Britain or other non-EU countries need an Animal Health Certificate instead of a passport. Entry from Serbia or Montenegro requires a rabies titre test.
- Croatia does not require tapeworm treatment for dogs entering from EU countries. Check your return country's rules, such as Ireland or Finland, before leaving.

## Insider Tips

- Book campsite or resort accommodation if beach access is the priority, since several dog beaches sit beside them.
- Carry a copy of the rabies certificate, which is required at Špadići.
- Pack a collapsible bowl and a cooling mat for summer. Shade is scarce on pebble beaches.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Poreč?

**Poreč is one of the most dog-friendly resort towns in Croatia, rated 8.5 out of 10.** It has around 12 dog beaches, a leash-friendly old town and near-universal acceptance in restaurants. The weak points are Blue Flag beaches that close to dogs, limited shade and a distant 24/7 emergency vet. Come in May, June or September and use the dog beaches rather than hunting for quiet coves.

faq.question: Does Poreč have an official dog beach?
faq.answer: Yes. Špadići Dog Beach, east of Zelena Laguna, opened on 7 June 2018 as the first official one. Brulo, Lanterna and Camp Istra are among the others, and about 12 dog beaches are promoted locally.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in restaurants in Poreč?
faq.answer: Mostly yes. Local tourism information says dogs are welcome in about 99% of restaurants, bars and shops. Terraces are the safest choice, and dogs are not allowed in supermarkets or food-prep areas.

faq.question: What documents does my dog need to drive into Croatia?
faq.answer: An ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination given after or on the day of chipping, and an EU pet passport. The first rabies vaccination must be at least 21 days old. Non-EU travellers need an Animal Health Certificate.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Poreč with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and early October. Temperatures are milder than in July and August, and the sea is still warm enough for swimming. Midsummer is possible if you walk in the early morning and evening.

faq.question: How much do hotels and apartments in Poreč charge for a dog?
faq.answer: Expect roughly €5 to €15 per night, with some cleaning fees on top. Campsites often charge €5 to €10 per day. Some private hosts allow dogs for free, so check the listing.

faq.question: Can dogs go on ferries and catamarans from Poreč?
faq.answer: Usually yes, on a leash and sometimes with a muzzle, but policy differs by operator. Some require a dog ticket or limit dogs to outdoor decks. Confirm in advance and carry the pet passport.

quickAnswer: Poreč is very dog-friendly. It has about a dozen dog beaches, including Špadići, Brulo and Lanterna. Dogs are welcome in most restaurants, cafés and shops and on the leashed waterfront. Blue Flag beaches are closed to dogs. Driving in requires an ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. Visit in spring or autumn.
